intent: Test sensor_size 0.016 on the confirmed baseline body (0.18 m, 0.8 kg) with the ±0.03 m, 15 mm-spaced array at y=0.04. Expect s-bend progress at or above 0.16 with line loss at or below 1, and a score at or above 52.1. Watch rms_error and steering_oscillation for signs that the larger footprint blurs the centring signal.
learning: Iteration 3 showed the lighter body (0.14 m, 0.6 kg) was the cause of the s-bend progress drop, not the ±0.03 m spread. Keep the baseline body. Sensor_size 0.016 is now the variable under test. If progress rises but rms_error or steering_oscillation worsens, the larger footprint is blurring the centring signal and the next step is to return to 0.012. If progress and line loss both hold, the next lever is the row position (y between 0.03 and 0.04) or a wider outer spread (x ±0.036), only if line loss stays at 2 on the slalom.
rationale: Iteration 3 has now raced. It kept the baseline body (0.18 m long, 0.8 kg) with the wider ±0.03 m spread at 15 mm spacing and the 4 cm row. Its s-bend progress was 0.16 with 1 line-loss event, against 0.1275 with 2 events for iteration 2. That isolates the drop to the lighter, shorter body, not to the spread, since the spread gave the 1 line-loss event. The rule set by the Integrator applies: progress at or above 0.15 with line loss at or below 1 means the body was the cause and the sensor_size 0.016 test is now appropriate. I therefore keep the baseline body and the ±0.03 m, y=0.04 array, and change sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 to cover more of the 25 mm tape at the edges. Expected result: s-bend line loss stays at or below 1, s-bend progress holds at 0.16 or rises, and the score is at or above the 52.1 of iteration 3. The main risk is that larger footprints blur the signal at small offsets and reduce centring precision, so rms_error and steering_oscillation are the measurements to watch. The off-track limit is still the 0.06 m floor for every allowed body width, so body width stays at 0.12 m. Wheel track, wheel radius and mass stay unchanged, so the only changes from iteration 3 are the sensor footprint size and the body reversion already confirmed.
